title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: bucket Cheon v2 (the accepted lead's own slack taken honestly: K = 0.51 and a 27-line itemisation charged at 150)

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target with auxiliary powers and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the deterministic algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic success probability at least 0.395 (at least 0.39 required). The success argument is the accepted lineage's law-based argument restated: 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39950 at K = 0.51 under H1 (the 6N^2(1 - (L-1)/L^2) independent rationals hit z = s^d like uniform elements of H, supported by Lemma 4, three coverage toys and an end-to-end run on a j = 0 curve), minus the eight cap tails C1-C8 (each computed here from scratch, every tail rounded towards the larger probability, together charged 2^-40) minus the 2^-20 C8 modelling budget. The cost is the exact-integer ledger W = 140608259479823067978322281977746804 target-group-operation units: records 2N x 2000 x (1 + 150/2000) at N = 65196422678611466571411401699906505 per side and the per-record charge 150 itemised over 27 lines (walk-side 30, three relay hops at 26, owner-side 17/11 against a maximal listing 125/119), plus the fifteen re-derived terms (per-node fixed, comparisons, gap tables, re-walk, strand and segment starts, status tree, walk list, base H-primes, split gaps, candidate multiplications, Lemma 1, kept blocks, candidate copy). Only A_1 and A_d are read, so the bound holds for every n >= 2^20. Score = ceil(10^6 log2 W)/10^6 = 116.759165, against the accepted lead's 116.793080; the 0.033915-bit gain is the lead's own published slack (K 0.51 vs 0.52, charge 150 vs 180) taken with a finer-grained itemisation, with every other parameter, the matching architecture and the heuristics restated and re-verified in this package.

experiments.purpose: One run, three modes. Mode ledger recomputes every size, term, cap tail, the exact integer memory sum and the exact score from integers and Fractions, asserting d | r-1, 6d | r-1, v2(r-1) = 32 and the H-prime density sanity (402 sixteenth powers below 2^16 against 408.875 expected); it outputs W = 140608259479823067978322281977746804 units, score 116.759165, the beats-lead integer comparison, the preprocessing split (baby side 2^115.7547, tables 2^97.03) and the memory block (per-owner-node 386142163104 bytes over 2^84 nodes, total 2^122.490 bytes). Mode coverage runs three scalar-level birthday toys (r = 134219713/536872321/2147492353 at d = 32/64/128, L = 60, chains sized for K = 0.51) measuring success against the diagonal-loss prediction 1 - e^{-K'} and reporting z-scores. Mode ec runs the whole attack end to end on the j = 0 curve y^2 = x^3 + 3 over F_207670579 of prime order r = 207671809 at d = 128: H-primes from a sieve, 15 chains of 25 steps per side, the 16-bit parity key routed to 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads, the bucket table with the whole baby side inserted first, equal-key candidates kept as (key, id, id'), the linear re-walk with the 4-step kept cap, the six GLV/negation candidates tested against the u-twisted A_d, the recovered z divided by the realised eigenvalue (resolved at setup against P0), the 7 square roots and the 128-root scan, asserting every recovered s equals the drawn secret. The full mode=all run completes in under 2 seconds and reproduces byte-identically from a foreign working directory.
